notes:
- Wide shots read right when a face that isn't one of the people is in the picture: a podcast's two hosts at a table with a screen behind them showing someone's face were read as one person, so the wide was never zoomed and the captions sat over the screen. People are now found by their faces and their bodies together, and a small face on a screen or poster no longer hides them.
- Fireside, Wraparound and Retention follow the wide-shot rule like every other format: in a wide, one centred line in the open gap between the people at head height (above their heads when the gap is too narrow), never on them, moving there on the frame of the cut.
